slides.title: AI is your pair programmer, not your replacement.
slides.html:
The big idea

AI is your pair programmer, not your replacement.

AI can write code fast, but you are responsible for every line you ship. This week you learn to use it well, and to check its work.

Full-Stack Development · Week 6 · AI-Assisted Development

slides.title: What AI can and can't do
slides.html:
AI tools

What AI can and can't do

Great at

Boilerplate, explaining code, spotting typos, suggesting fixes, writing first drafts.

Gets wrong

Outdated APIs, made-up functions, missing edge cases, confident wrong answers.

Never share

Passwords, API keys, .env files or other people's private data.

Tools: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Cursor

slides.title: Writing clear, specific prompts
slides.html:
Prompts

Writing clear, specific prompts

❌ Vague

make a login page

✅ Specific

I'm building a React (Vite) app with plain CSS.
Create a LoginForm component with email and
password inputs, client-side validation (email
must contain @, password 8+ chars), an error
message under each field, and a submit button
that is disabled while submitting. Explain each
part in simple terms.

Context: your stack

Goal: what it should do

Constraints

Format: explain it

slides.title: A prompt formula that works
slides.html:
Prompts

A prompt formula that works

1

Context

What you're building and with what: "React + Vite, no Tailwind"

2

Task

Exactly what you want: "a component that…"

3

Details

Inputs, rules, edge cases, how it should look

4

Format

"Explain line by line", "only show the changed code", "give me 2 options"

5

Iterate

Follow up: "make it accessible", "simplify this", "why did you use useEffect?"

slides.title: Reading AI code line by line
slides.html:
Read it

Reading AI code line by line

  • Never paste code you can't explain
  • Ask: what does each line do? why this way?
  • Look up anything unfamiliar
  • Rename things so they make sense to you

Review

// AI wrote this. Can you explain every line?
const visible = jobs
  .filter((j) => j.title.toLowerCase().includes(q))
  .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt - a.createdAt)
  .slice(0, 20);
 
// 1. keep jobs whose title contains the search
// 2. newest first
// 3. only the first 20
// If you can't write these comments, ask the AI.

slides.title: Debugging errors with AI
slides.html:
Debug

Debugging errors with AI

  • Give the AI the full error message
  • Paste the code where it happens
  • Say what you expected and what happened
  • Ask why, not just for a fix

A good debugging prompt

My React app crashes with:
 
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined
(reading 'map') at JobList.jsx:12
 
Here is JobList.jsx: [paste code]
jobs comes from an API fetch in App.jsx.
I expected an empty list while loading.
Why does this happen and how do I fix it?

slides.title: Improving existing features
slides.html:
Refactor

Improving existing features

  • Ask AI to review your code like a senior dev
  • Ask for one improvement at a time
  • Keep your app working after each change
  • Commit before you let AI change things

A refactoring prompt

Review this component like a senior React
developer. List problems with readability,
performance and accessibility, ranked by
importance. Don't rewrite it yet.
 
[paste component]
 
Then: "Apply only suggestion 1 and explain
the change."

slides.title: If you didn't test it, it doesn't work.
slides.html:
Verify

If you didn't test it, it doesn't work.

AI code often looks right and still fails. Run it, click everything, try strange input, and read the console before you trust it.

Full-Stack Development · Week 6 · AI-Assisted Development

slides.title: Testing AI-generated code
slides.html:
Verify

Testing AI-generated code

1

Run it

Does it load without errors in the console?

2

Happy path

Does the main feature work the normal way?

3

Edge cases

Empty input, very long text, no internet, double clicks

4

Different screens

Phone, tablet, laptop in DevTools device mode

5

Explain it

Could you explain it to a classmate? If not, ask until you can

slides.title: Your frontend mini project
slides.html:
Week 6 build

Your frontend mini project

01

Plan

Problem, users, 3 core features, a sketch of each screen and the data you'll store.

02

Build with AI

React + Router + state + an API or localStorage. Use AI, but understand every line.

03

Present

A 3-minute demo: the problem, a live walkthrough, one thing AI got wrong and how you fixed it.

Deliver: live link, GitHub repo with README, and a 3-minute demo

slides.title: Your project README
slides.html:
Build

Your project README

  • Every project needs a clear README
  • Recruiters read it before your code
  • Include what you used AI for

README.md

# Study Timer
 
A Pomodoro timer for students, built with React.
 
**Live:** https://study-timer.netlify.app
 
## Features
- 25/5 minute focus and break sessions
- Sessions saved in localStorage
- Works on phones
 
## How I used AI
Generated the timer hook, then fixed a bug
where the timer kept running after pausing.
